##### Project general facts

Salt of Virgin Beach is a beachfront hospitality investment located in one of Bali’s last untouched coastal areas, offering direct access to Virgin Beach and unobstructed ocean views. The project is designed as a high-end resort with a strong focus on sustainability, architectural integrity, and premium guest experience. Its secluded location and limited surrounding development create long-term value through scarcity and high positioning in the luxury segment. For investors, Salt of Virgin Beach represents a rare opportunity to enter an emerging destination with strong upside potential, stable demand growth, and long-term capital appreciation.

The project appears to be designed as a lifestyle retreat with a strong resort atmosphere. Visuals suggest curated leisure and wellness spaces, beachfront relaxation areas, and hospitality services operated by an international hotel management group. Residents and guests benefit from direct beach access and a setting designed around nature, ocean views, and a relaxed coastal lifestyle.

The interiors, based on the design style shown in the visuals, emphasize warm natural tones, wood textures, and open layouts that complement the tropical environment. Residences are designed to feel airy and connected to the outdoors through large windows and spacious terraces. The overall interior concept reflects high-quality finishes with modern materials, focusing on calm, resort-inspired living spaces.

##### Parking

Shared Parking.

##### Location description and benefits

Karangasem Regency is one of the most scenic and culturally rich regions on the eastern side of Bali. Known for its dramatic coastline, volcanic mountains, and traditional villages, the area offers a more authentic and tranquil side of the island compared to the busy southern districts. Its landscape combines black-sand beaches, lush hills, and views of the iconic Mount Agung, creating a striking natural setting that attracts travelers and residents seeking privacy, nature, and cultural depth.

One of Karangasem’s key advantages is its access to some of Bali’s most iconic natural and cultural landmarks. The region is home to historic water palaces such as Tirta Gangga and Taman Ujung, as well as world-class diving and snorkeling spots around Amed and Tulamben. These attractions, combined with untouched beaches and quiet coastal villages, make the area a unique destination for nature lovers, divers, and those seeking a slower, more immersive island lifestyle.

Karangasem is also gaining attention as an emerging location for boutique resorts and private villas, thanks to its preserved landscapes and lower development density compared to southern Bali. Improved infrastructure and road connections make it increasingly accessible from Ngurah Rai International Airport, while the region still maintains a peaceful, authentic atmosphere. This balance between natural beauty, cultural heritage, and growing accessibility positions Karangasem as a promising destination for both lifestyle living and long-term investment in Bali.
